query: Many physical and chemical fabrication approaches have produced multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles, yet their synthesis–structure–property relationships remain poorly established. This limits evaluation of their suitability for catalytic operation at 773–1173 K and thermoelectric use at 473–1923 K, including catalytic settings where low noble-metal content is desirable. What governs whether these nanoparticles preserve structural and chemical stability under such service regimes, and why? Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis, specify a controlled intervention that separates it from competing explanations, predict observations relative to a baseline, define its boundary conditions, connect it to the prior evidence summarized above, and provide a clear falsification test.

generation.hypothesis: In near-equiatomic, multi-element solid-solution nanoparticles, the elastic strain energy from atomic size mismatch (δ) can exceed the configurational entropy stabilization at service temperatures (~773–1173 K), driving phase separation and surface segregation; only compositions with δ below a critical threshold (≈5 %) remain single-phase and chemically homogeneous under these conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: As-synthesized near-equiatomic, single-phase solid-solution nanoparticles (5–20 nm diameter) with defined atomic radius mismatch δ
generation.intervention: Select two equiatomic quinary nanoparticle compositions differing only in δ (low δ≈3 % vs. high δ≈8 %), then anneal both at 1073 K for 10 h under inert Ar atmosphere
generation.conditions: Particle size 5–20 nm; inert (Ar) atmosphere; 1073 K; 10 h; quinary FCC elements
generation.structural_mediator: Elastic strain energy associated with atomic size mismatch δ
generation.mechanism: For high δ, elastic strain energy adds to positive mixing enthalpy, overcoming T·ΔSmix and triggering phase separation and surface segregation of mismatched atoms; for low δ this penalty remains below T·ΔSmix, so the solid solution stays stable
generation.predicted_outcome: Low-δ nanoparticles remain single-phase and compositionally uniform; high-δ nanoparticles exhibit phase separation (new peaks in XRD) and elemental segregation at particle surfaces (observed by STEM-EDS and APT) relative to baseline
generation.baseline: Both compositions start as single-phase, compositionally homogeneous solid-solution nanoparticles pre-annealing
generation.boundary: Holds for FCC near-equiatomic quinary alloys sized 5–20 nm in inert atmospheres at 773–1173 K; may not apply to bcc alloys, δ outside 0–10 %, particle sizes >50 nm, or reactive gas environments
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: the exact critical δ threshold and its temperature dependence may shift with specific element combinations and particle size

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize the two equiatomic nanoparticle compositions (δ≈3 % and δ≈8 %), anneal both at 1073 K for 10 h in Ar, then characterize phase and composition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the high-δ (≈8 %) nanoparticles remain single-phase and homogeneous after annealing under the specified conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
